If you feel like you're hitting a plateau, you could try going down to 15-1600 calories, longer or more frequent workouts, or mixing in more cardio with your lifting. If your goal is to lose bodyfat in a short period whilst not losing muscle I would suggest more HIIT training like rope skipping, interval sprinting, etc. These also train your abs so that's a bonus. Do these exercises between your sets to keep a very high heart rate and end with 2 or 3 to keep burning calories for a time after your training. Of course counting calories is vital, looking through this topic I recommend dropping cards in favor of protein to stimulate muscle growth.

A few tips:

  • Let your diet do the work. I can't stress this enough. Drop it down to 1500 Cals and do less cardio. If you must stay active do something really low intensity like going for a walk.

  • At the gym: Keep the same weight, but lower the volume. That means less reps and/or sets. Again, your diet is doing the work, so your goal at the gym is simply to maintain lean body mass while the fat melts away.

  • Being on a caloric deficit impairs your ability to recover, so do no more than 2-3 full body workouts per week.

  • Diet: Low carb on off-days, and moderate carb intake on workout days. High protein every day.

I know it's tempting to work your butt off during a cut, but honestly it's better (and easier, IMO) to do less, relax, and let the deficit do the majority of the work. The hardest part is the psychological: controlling your hunger and staying away from triggers that cause you to overeat.

Now I am second guessing myself again. Not that I am really doing that much cardio but I was under the impression (especially given what was said here) that a little more cardio would be helpful especially of the HIIT variety since it supposedly"burns" less muscle. I have lowered my daily calorie intake a smidgen over the last few days (1590ish) but I'm curious what you consider to be low carb - 100g? less?

I consider low carb to be 100 g. You can go lower, but you'll end up with a diet consisting mostly of meat and fat, which I personally find disagreeable. As far as the cardio goes, it helps you burn calories, yes, which is the goal, but you can get the same result by eating less. You can burn 100 Cals doing exercise or you can eat 100 Cals less, right? The reason I prefer eating less is because exercise becomes incredibly taxing both physically and mentally when on a prolonged caloric deficit. Hunger pangs increase, motivation drops, you may retain water, your body basically starts sabotaging you; exercise makes it worse. Your goal in the gym is simply to try to maintain strength and lean body mass, that's it. The rest of your efforts are better spent cooking, planning your meals, and keeping your mind busy.
